And it did so fairly quickly this time. But, still, I cannot forcibly reproduce it. It has been a few days since it crashed. So, in total, it ran for dozens upon dozens of hours without crashing but this time it crashed within an hour.

> Godot for UI/UX) will randomly crash. It happens rarely. Maybe... once every 10 hours of the application being active.

> X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (nvidia; 550.135)

1. you run Nvidia on x11 in Vulkan - Nvidia driver have unsolved bugs/conflicts with Vulkan-x11 interaction.
2. you run "very old" Nvidia driver - latest is 565.77 - that support Wayland correctly (but even 565.77 still randomly crash with any Vulkan games)
3. you run OpenGL3 compatibility ........................................... its 2025 ..... stop
4. Godot to render single frame use 3+ framebuffers - and there(in OpenGL overal, and you have on top of it outdated x11) alot-alot bugs/crashes related to "start-stop" rendering with complex multi framebuffer rendering pipeline.
5. **by using game engine to render UI-app - it extremely counter productive way - it use GPU to render entire UI-screen 60+FPS every second -because game engines expect to render games full frame, not UI** - when even Electron render UI much more effective - you waste "electricity/performance/vram memory" by using game engine for UI app - it bad.
6. Nvidia does not fix any x11 bugs, and do not fix any OpenGL bugs - time to update. (and rewrite your app to something that fit your use case like Electron)
7. This is 100% Nvidia bug, not Godot bug - **you must test your "app" on more than single GPU to know for sure is it Godot-engine bug or its single GPU driver.**
> While in the background, the application is mostly paused, in a deep sleep. With rendering being paused entirely. I do this by assigning a signal to FocusExited and FocusEntered of the main window of course.

Re-start GPU rendering is still insanely expensive/slow - especially on laptop or smartphones and especially on full-screen(large) window-apps - you still burning battery for no reason. (and there alot of OpenGL bugs/crashes related to start/stop rendering with complex pipeline with framebuffers)

Even Electron will work like 1000x more effective by energy/performance usage for UI app than Godot..

> 
> > X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1050 Ti (nvidia; 550.135)

And Electron uses a quadrillion GB of memory to even render a single button, causes applications to require about 5 full SSDs of storage space. And... well, suffice it to say, I have a reason to use a game engine for an app. Why judge it? And, what I use Godot for is not your business anyhow.

look there - one of "wontfix" Nvidia bugs in x11 - https://github.com/KhronosGroup/Vulkan-Samples/issues/250#issuecomment-868021052 - very similar to your case - Nvidia driver or x11 somehow wrong communicate and send frames on "framebuffer stop-recreation"(on resize that happens) - it happens there once per few hundred resizes - but it intense recreation every frame - you need to be lucky to hit "the unsync frame"

> It's not an nVidia bug.

it is - and there nothing you can do about it because Nvidia driver is proprietary.

it just trigger rare case by running it for long.
Godot by using multiple framebuffers - and stopping them/running - same - it broken on driver level.
(and at beginning - **consumer GPU have non-ECC VRAM - no one guarantee it work stable for "long time"**)

It impossible to "prove" is it software-logic bug or hardware or driver - for software that run for hours on consumer-tier hardware.
Consumer tier PC not designed to run software for hours "stable".

> Who says I haven't? It's showing the same behavior on an aging laptop with an Intel APU.

Unity engine will crash every ~24 hours (in intense use) no matter what you do - because this how Mono garbage collector works - start stop "world simulation" to clean object then repeat - huge ram segmentation - intense ram usage - crash - not software problems and there no way to fix it - it just not made to be used this way - it game engine.

In context of Godot - Godot engine 4.x any version - "OpenGL compatibility" - crash SteamDeck SteamOS (and any Linux with AMD GPU) in 10-20 mins - because - how broken AMD OpenGL diver - and no one will fix it. (you lucky OpenGL works for hours on Nvidia GPU - drivers there "not too bad" but OpenGL just broken - no one updating or fixing OpenGL drivers for 6+ years already opensource or proprietary) 

> Please, stop responding if you have nothing constructive to say. You know, you're being reported to the CoC.

First to "prove" that is software bug - you need full ECC RAM and enterprise level GPU with ECC VRAM.
Second - latest driver on officially supported linux kernel stable version.
Third - not using OpenGL that is impossible to debug - no one fixing OpenGL bugs even in opensource drivers anymore. (thinking Nvidia devs will spend their time debugging OpenGL rare case....)
Fourth - do not use x11 but use Wayland.

Your app touch 3 very bugged technology - OpenGL, x11, Nvidia driver on consumer GPUs.

@danilw I assume you wanted to be helpful, but the tone you used and the kind of information you provided to this user reporting a bug was quite condescending and unconstructive. I'd like to remind you of the Godot [Code of Conduct](https://godotengine.org/code-of-conduct/), and remind that if you want to help with issue triage, you need to make sure that this is done in a way that is professional, friendly and constructive.

I read your comments as almost _blaming_ the user for just trying to use Godot the way it's designed, and running into some bugs. It doesn't matter whether the bugs are the fault of Nvidia, X11, Vulkan, OpenGL, or any other component. It's a crash that affects Godot and thus it's our responsibility to debug it and figure out where the fault actually lies (not just make some assumptions as you did), and see if we can work it around if we can't fix the bug.

In this case the closest known bug is https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/xorg/lib/libx11/-/issues/199 which has a Godot counterpart here, so this issue can be closed as duplicate of it: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/75308

A lot of the statements you made are off-topic and not at all related to the problem at hand. They're distracting at best, offensive at worst, when you tell the user they're using Godot wrong and should use Electron. The fact that this user deleted their GitHub account after interacting with you should give a hint as how they received your input on their bug report.
